annotations.label: energy-based model
annotations.short: A model that assigns lower energy to configurations it considers more probable.
annotations.details: Instead of parameterizing probability directly, the model defines an energy $E_\theta(x)$ and turns negative energy into an unnormalized probability through an exponential.

annotations.label: $\theta$
annotations.short: The trainable parameters $\theta$ of the probability model $p_\theta$.
annotations.details: Changing $\theta$ changes the energy function, and therefore changes the probability assigned to $x$. The same annotation ID is reused for multiple occurrences because the parameter has the same role.

annotations.label: $E_\theta(x)$
annotations.short: The energy $E_\theta(x)$ assigned to $x$ by parameters $\theta$; lower energy means larger unnormalized probability.
annotations.details: The exponential $e^{-E_\theta(x)}$ converts energy into a positive score. This score still needs normalization by $Z_\theta$.

annotations.label: $Z_\theta$
annotations.short: The partition function $Z_\theta$: the normalization constant for $p_\theta(x)$.
annotations.details: $Z_\theta$ sums or integrates $e^{-E_\theta(x)}$ over all possible $x$ so the resulting probabilities sum or integrate to one.

annotations.label: partition function
annotations.short: The quantity that turns the model's unnormalized scores into a valid probability distribution.
annotations.details: Without dividing by the partition function, $e^{-E_\theta(x)}$ is only proportional to a probability density.

annotations.label: $\nabla_\theta \log p_\theta(x)$
annotations.short: The gradient $\nabla_\theta \log p_\theta(x)$ of log probability with respect to the model parameters $\theta$.
annotations.details: It points in the direction of greatest local increase of $\log p_\theta(x)$ and is a basic ingredient of gradient-based maximum-likelihood training.

annotations.label: energy landscape
annotations.short: A visualization of how the model's energy varies over possible inputs $x$.
annotations.details: Low regions of the curve correspond to configurations with larger unnormalized probability $e^{-E_\theta(x)}$.

Gibbs.short: A Gibbs/Boltzmann-style distribution assigns probability proportional to ^{-E(x)}$ for an energy function $.
Gibbs.details: Lower-energy configurations receive exponentially larger probability. The proportionality constant is the partition function.
